claims.statement: Both production-facing simulation reads (`replay` and `auditDrift`) run in the desktop main process against the saved model resolved by `modelSourceOf` (`<root>/.evidence/fm` or a bundle path), never against the unsaved canvas, because the audit must describe what was saved and deployed; `runNativeDriftAudit` re-reads the model for each call rather than taking it from a session.

`readProductionTrace` turns a span into an `EvidenceCommit` only when the span carries a non-empty `fm.evidence.ref` and a `traceId`/`spanId`: spans without the ref are skipped silently as context, a span that names Evidence but lacks ids produces a `path: ...` error and is dropped while the rest of the trace is still read, and the resulting commits are ordered by `startTimeUnixNano` then `spanId`.

The trace reader understands exactly `fm.evidence.ref`, `fm.context.ref`, `fm.fulfillment.request.ref`, `fm.fulfillment.status`, any `fm.value.*` (prefix stripped into `values`) and `service.name`, where a span-level service name overrides the resource-level one, an unknown fulfillment status collapses the claim to `null`, and an OTLP `intValue` string is converted with `Number` so numeric comparisons against modeled values work.

The drift vocabulary is five kinds with severity fixed per kind: `UNMODELED_EVIDENCE_COMMITTED` and `DERIVED_VALUE_SUPPLIED` are `block`; `UNMODELED_ATTRIBUTE_WRITTEN`, `CROSS_CONTEXT_WRITE` and `BREACH_WITHOUT_FOLLOW_UP` are `warn`.

A commit whose `fm.evidence.ref` is absent from the model, or resolves to a non-Evidence entity such as a context or role, is reported as `UNMODELED_EVIDENCE_COMMITTED` and short-circuits the remaining checks for that commit.

`CROSS_CONTEXT_WRITE` is raised only when the commit itself states a `fm.context.ref` that differs from the entity's modeled context, and it carries distinct messages for a modeled context written by the wrong service versus a context the model never declared.

`DERIVED_VALUE_SUPPLIED` requires the written attribute to be declared on the entity and to carry `derivedByRuleRef`, and is skipped when the written value is `null` or `undefined`, so a modeled-but-empty derived field is tolerated.

`BREACH_WITHOUT_FOLLOW_UP` is raised when a `breached` fulfillment references a request that has no model breach rule, or when no other commit in the breached request's context (different Evidence ref, not one of the rule's confirmation bindings) follows it — a deliberately tolerant check, since the compensation may be recorded in another team's trace.

Every drift finding carries the commit pointer (`traceId`, `spanId`, `serviceName`, `operation`, `at`), `evidenceRef`, `contextRef`, a `modelExpectation` naming the expected rule or context, a business-worded `remediation`, and a `driftId` derived deterministically from kind, ref, trace/span and message.

`DriftAudit.passed` means only "no blocking finding", not "the trace was readable": a non-OTLP or unparsed document yields `passed: true` with no findings and an `errors` entry, and `runNativeDriftAudit` merges model source issues into that same de-duplicated error list.

`driftIssues` converts audit findings into `SensorIssue`s tagged `source: 'audit_drift'`, keeping severity, using the kind as `code`, `evidenceRef` as `targetNodeId`, `contextRef`, and the remediation as `suggestion`, and turns each audit error into a `warn` `DRIFT_TRACE_UNREADABLE` so an unreadable trace cannot pass as a clean audit.

`buildSensorReport` accepts an optional drift report, folds it after the FM check and key-data ledger, and `finalizeSensorReport` de-duplicates by `issueId` and recomputes `passed` and `isStageGateReady`, so one blocking drift fails the report; no ordinary desktop sensor run supplies a drift report, which reaches users through the radar and the MCP tool instead.

`decideGovernance` maps each drift kind to exactly one action and tool: `UNMODELED_EVIDENCE_COMMITTED` to `adopt_production_change` via `roleify_and_invert_dependency`, `UNMODELED_ATTRIBUTE_WRITTEN` to `adopt_production_change` via `apply_model_patch`, `BREACH_WITHOUT_FOLLOW_UP` to `close_compensation_gap` via `add_breach_compensation`, `CROSS_CONTEXT_WRITE` to `move_write_to_owner` via `apply_model_patch`, and `DERIVED_VALUE_SUPPLIED` as well as any unknown kind to `raise_blocking_ticket` with a `null` tool because it is a person's decision.

The governance verdict is ranked `production_overreach` over `needs_repair` over `model_lagging` over `healthy`, and a replay with `passedCount < scenarioCount` appends a `repair_model` action using the agent's `run_sensors` tool without outranking a production overreach.

`canPatchModel` requires no blocking drift, a supplied replay that did not fail, and a `model_lagging` verdict — so a `healthy` verdict also disables patching, and a failing replay closes the patch path because the repair would otherwise be built on a broken baseline.

`GOVERNANCE_PROMPT` is the reverse-direction turn — read the trace with `audit_production_drift` and the replay, keep `block` and `warn` distinct, let the model move for unmodeled facts and breach gaps, refuse model edits for supplied derived values and cross-context writes, patch only through `apply_model_patch` and the existing operators, re-run the replay afterwards, and report what was adopted, refused and deferred — and `GOVERNANCE_INSTRUCTIONS` composes it with the role, modeling and operator sections in place of the workshop workflow, which the desktop runtime does not select.

`registerSimulationIpc` answers replay, drift and trace-dialog channels through the same `createSimulationService` factory the MCP tools use; the drift channel reads the picked file and `JSON.parse`s it in the main process, so a non-JSON trace rejects with a `不是 JSON` error and the audit service is never called.

`useSimulationReplay` holds a frame cursor rather than a timer (0 on a new reply with frames, -1 otherwise), clamps at both ends, and drops replies from an earlier load, so stepping forward twice always shows the same two frames.
`useDriftAudit` owns `{audit, tracePath, loading, error}` and a cancelled trace picker returns without calling the drift channel, so the previous audit stays on screen.

`SimulationSandbox` is one dialog with a replay tab and a production-drift tab: the replay side lists scenario summaries and per-frame acting role, instance, derivations, fulfillment states and checkpoints with a locate-on-canvas action, while the drift side shows per finding a severity badge, the localized kind label, the evidence ref, the message and the remediation, omitting `contextRef` and `modelExpectation`.

`audit_production_drift` is a read-only MCP tool whose input is an already-parsed OTLP/JSON document rather than a path; the main process resolves the active project root through `get_app_state` and refuses with `NO_ACTIVE_PROJECT` when nothing is open.

The agent-facing projection `driftOf` keeps `modelId`, span and commit counts, `counts`, each finding's kind, severity, message, evidenceRef, contextRef and remediation, plus `passed` and `errors`, dropping `driftId`, the commit pointer and `modelExpectation`.
Both simulation reads degrade instead of throwing: an unreadable model directory yields `passed: false` with the read error in `errors` for replay and for the drift audit.

`apps/desktop/src/main/governanceLoop.spec.ts` proves the loop end to end on the traceable-subscription fixture: sandbox frames walk a payment from pending to completed, a matching trace yields verdict `healthy` with `canPatchModel: false`, a service-written `expired_at` yields `production_overreach` with a null-tool ticket, and a breach with no follow-up yields `model_lagging` with `add_breach_compensation`.
